event: Federal Decree-Law No. (32) of 2025 (the CMA replaces and renames the SCA, Art. 2(2) and (3); in force under Art. 30) and Federal Decree-Law No. (33) of 2025 on the Regulation of the Capital Market (issued 1 October 2025; in force under Art. 85) enter into force. FDL 33 defines Virtual Assets (Art. 1), lists Promotion (Art. 3(1)(i)) and activities and services related to Virtual Assets (Art. 3(1)(y)) as licensable, reaches any person targeting clients within the State (Art. 2(1)(d)), excludes Financial Free Zones and Central Bank-licensed activities (Art. 2(4)), ties trading to an official list plus CMA registration (Art. 39) and gives one year to adjust status, extendable by the Board (Art. 83). FDL 32 Art. 27(3) keeps Cabinet Resolutions 111 and 112 of 2022 in force until replaced.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. A UAE-federal opinion dated on or after 1 January 2026 names the CMA, not the SCA, and reads FDL 33 Arts 2(1)(d), 3 and 39. An earlier opinion cites the SCA and the 2022 Cabinet Resolutions, which stay in force until repealed, amended or replaced. The Art. 83 adjustment period runs to 1 January 2027 by arithmetic and the Board may extend it.

event: Resolution No. (04/Chairman) of 2026 Concerning the Regulation of Virtual Assets Service Providers and the Alternative Trading System Operator (also cited as 4/R.M of 2026). Board approval 26 December 2025; issued 13 February 2026; Official Gazette 27 February 2026; in force 28 February 2026 (Art. 7, the day after publication). Three modules (Art. 1), a one-year regularisation period (Art. 3), and Art. 6 repeals Decision No. (26/Chairman) of 2023 and the Rulebook VASP provisions. The General Module's Art. 12 lists eight financial activities. The record sits on the CMA Rulebook; it is not on the CMA's Latest Regulations page, which listed only Decisions 11 and 13 and Resolutions 16 and 18 of 2026 on 16 October 2026.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. An opinion on CMA-perimeter VASP activity dated on or after 28 February 2026 reads this resolution, not Decision 26/2023; one dated before it read the 2023 decision and needs re-reading. The one-year regularisation period under Art. 3 is a dated fact to check.

event: Press release: the CMA issues the Virtual Assets Framework, five core modules (General Requirements; Conduct of Business; Alternative Trading System; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing; Prudential Requirements) and eight regulated activities, expanded from three. The release names no decision number and no effective date. Commentators identify the framework with Resolution 04/2026; the CMA does not say so.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. An activity mapping written against the earlier regime's three activities needs re-reading against eight. The release itself fixes no date.

event: Resolution No. (16/Chairman) of 2026 (Board approval 9 June 2026; in force on issuance): entities licensed by the Central Bank, other than insurance companies, may practise the activities under Resolution 04/2026.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. Banks and payment firms can be federal virtual-asset activity providers, so the set of counterparties an opinion may name widens. Not a marketing instrument.

event: Regulations on the Marketing of Virtual Assets and Related Activities 2024, current version, effective from 1 October 2024.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. A standing fact for any Dubai-facing communication an opinion describes; stated here, not applied.

event: Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook, current version (cover 19 May 2025; site: effective 19 June 2025). Category 1 issuance needs a VARA licence; Category 2 needs no licence but all placement and distribution runs through a Licensed Distributor (Rule I.E.1), and no Category 2 asset is deemed approved by VARA (Rule I.E.5); Exempt VAs have no prior requirement. Annex 2 (asset-referenced virtual assets): a legal opinion from a duly registered lawyer "may be required" (Rule III.B.2) and "shall be required" for ARVA issuers holding Reserve Assets (Rule III.C.4). The 7 February 2023, 19 September 2023 and 1 October 2024 versions had no Annex 2.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. A Dubai issuance opinion dated after 19 June 2025 categorises the issuance under this version. The lawyer-signed opinion rule exists only for ARVAs under Annex 2.

event: Exchange Services Rulebook effective (prior versions 7 February 2023 and 19 May 2025); Part V adds the exchange-traded derivatives rules.
effect_on_opinion: Date. An opinion on Dubai exchange services dated before 31 March 2026 predates the derivatives rules.

event: Guidance on the Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook (indicative under Regulation I.B.4). Items 32 and 34, on Annex 2 opinions: the opinion is prepared and signed by a "duly registered practising lawyer", not the issuer's internal counsel; it is dated, signed and on letterhead; it states its assumptions and sources; a revised or supplemental opinion follows any material change. Example D: a 15 Working Day Submission Period for Category 2 distributions, and VARA's silence is not approval. The date is from the PDF cover and the revision feed (at least 12 entries dated 9 April 2026); the HTML pages are undated.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. For ARVA issuances the signer, form and currency expectations are now written down; an undated or in-house opinion falls outside the guidance. The guidance calls itself indicative and no substitute for independent legal advice.

event: Federal AML/CFT Laws page updated (revision feed). Only this feed entry is verified; earlier feed dates are not.
effect_on_opinion: Date. AML references in an opinion point at the May 2026 version.

event: AML/CFT Business Risk Assessment Guidance published.
effect_on_opinion: Context for a VASP's own file. No effect on the form of a legal opinion.

event: Notices of Fines on the regulatory notices page: CoinMENA FZE and MX Global LTD (MEXC) on 22 June 2026, Peken Global Limited (KuCoin) on 24 June 2026, Shelbit General Trading L.L.C on 24 July 2026. Amounts are not on the listing page.
effect_on_opinion: Date. Where a counterparty's status matters, a relier reads the notices page as of the opinion's date and again as of the date of reliance.

event: Circular regarding Reserve Assets Audit Report: minimum expectations for the independent audit of Reserve Assets after a thematic review of 2025 reports. Not about legal opinions.
effect_on_opinion: Context. Assurance expectations for custodians and exchanges rise; no change to the form of an opinion.

event: Public register snapshot: 59 licensed VASPs, every entry Active with licence type VASP Licence; newest licence 6 October 2026 (Payward FZCO, VL/26/10/002), after Rain MENA FZE on 5 October 2026 (VL/26/10/001); earliest 28 July 2023 (Laser Digital Middle East FZE). The register states that applicants holding an In-Principle Approval are strictly prohibited from initiating operations.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The register row a relier checks against a credential's as-of date. The count read 57 on 11 October 2026 and 59 on 16 October 2026, and will move again; it is re-read each edition.

event: Joint Guidelines JC 2024 28 under MiCA Art. 97 (apply from 12 May 2025): Annex A, the explanation for Art. 8(4); Annex B, the legal-opinion template for asset-referenced tokens under Arts 17(1)(b)(ii) and 18(2)(e); Annex C, the standardised test. Paragraph 16 lets an in-house or external legal adviser complete the opinion.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. An ART opinion follows the Annex B field list: date issued, the adviser's evidence of ability, a conflicts declaration, the dated final white paper attached, Member States, applicable law. The template has no expiry and names no reliers. MiCA asks for a legal opinion only for asset-referenced tokens.

event: Final report on the reverse-solicitation guidelines (ESMA35-1872330276-1899): the Art. 61 exemption is "very narrowly framed"; Art. 61(2) bars marketing new types of crypto-assets or services on the back of a client's own initiative.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The reverse-solicitation position in an EU opinion is an as-of judgment under these guidelines.

event: Statement on MiCA transitional measures (ESMA75-453128700-1396): where a CASP obtains authorisation in one Member State after a shorter transitional period has ended in another, an interim period of up to six months can arise in which it lacks the authorisation to serve clients there.
effect_on_opinion: Date. Shows why an opinion's date matters more than its jurisdiction label during a transition.

event: The CASP provisions of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 apply (Art. 149(2)). Art. 143(3): a provider operating lawfully before this date may continue until 1 July 2026 or until authorisation is granted or refused, whichever is sooner, and Member States may shorten the period; Art. 143(6): a simplified procedure for applications made between 30 December 2024 and 1 July 2026; Art. 110: ESMA's register of non-compliant entities.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The baseline date for every EU row and the start of the edition window.

event: Guidelines on the qualification of crypto-assets as financial instruments (ESMA75453128700-1323), applying 60 days after publication of the translations: substance over form; three cumulative criteria for transferable securities; the examples are not a definitive classification.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The Art. 2(5) classification in an EU opinion is an as-of judgment under these guidelines; an opinion predating them was written against no common test.

event: Statement on the end of the transitional periods (ESMA75-113276571-1631): unauthorised CASPs keep wind-down plans ready; national authorities treat last-minute applications with considerable caution. ESMA Q&A 2220 (4 July 2024): a pending application does not extend the right to operate past the national cut-off.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A counterparty still in the queue after its national cut-off is unauthorised, and an opinion says so as of its date.

event: Ireland's 12-month transitional period ended (the same page also prints 31 December 2025).
effect_on_opinion: Date. A national cut-off example; both dates are printed until the Bank reconciles them.

event: Statement (ESMA75-113276571-1679): the transitional period expires across the EU on 1 July 2026, whether or not MiCA has been implemented in a Member State; after that date an unauthorised provider must cease.
effect_on_opinion: Date. Fixes the EU-wide date.

event: Public statement (ESMA75-113276571-1710): unauthorised CASPs stop onboarding EU clients and wind down; some significant providers may not be authorised by the deadline.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A counterparty's status on 1 July 2026 is a dated fact an opinion pins.

event: End of the CASP transitional backstop. National periods per ESMA's list (file dated 19 May 2026): six EU states used 6 months (Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Slovenia, Finland; ended 30 June 2025 by LEXI's arithmetic); five used 12 months (Germany, Ireland, Lithuania, Austria, Slovakia; ended 30 December 2025); Norway (EEA) 12 months; Sweden 9 months; the rest 18 months. Application deadlines stated in the list: Bulgaria before 8 October 2025 for VASP-registered entities, Czechia before 31 July 2025, Denmark before 30 December 2024, Italy by 30 December 2025. ESMA warns that some periods may not have been incorporated into national law yet. No deadline is attributed to Belgium.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. An EU-scope opinion dated after 1 July 2026 cannot rest on a national VASP registration. A relier checks the ESMA register row's authorisation date against the credential's as-of date.

event: The AMF reports 31 CASPs authorised in France and 283 in the EU as of early July 2026, with a few authorisations being finalised.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A national data point on the AMF's own date, never presented as an ESMA figure.

event: Response to the MiCA review: the press release reports 39 e-money tokens issued and no asset-referenced tokens authorised as at 1 September 2026; the response itself notes product launches delayed by protracted processes involving legal opinions and supervisory dialogues to establish regulatory classification.
effect_on_opinion: Context. Annex B legal opinions are rare in practice as of that date.

event: Response to the MiCA review (ESMA75-113276571-1721): proposals for binding ESMA opinions on token classification, simplified white-paper notification procedures, stricter marketing rules including for promotion by influencers, reinforced supervisory powers over third-country firms soliciting EU investors, and explicit rules against regulated firms offering services linked to non-compliant stablecoins.
effect_on_opinion: Date. Classification judgments in current opinions may be superseded by Level 1 change; the as-of date carries that risk.

event: Interim MiCA register snapshot: 370 CASP rows (367 distinct names) across 27 home states (24 EU Member States plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; Hungary, Poland and Romania have no rows); 173 non-compliant entity rows (Italy 164, Belgium 6, Czechia 1, the Netherlands 1, Slovakia 1; last update 16 September 2026). Weekly updates; one row carries a 2028 date.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The two lists a relier checks in one visit; a credential names which list was checked and when.

event: Opinion (ESMA75-113276571-1742): CASPs should cease providing services related to non-MiCA-compliant asset-referenced and e-money tokens to EU clients; national authorities should require remediation of remaining pre-existing exposures no later than three months after the opinion's publication; any continuation is limited to liquidation, conversion, withdrawal, transfer or safekeeping and stays time-limited and supervised.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A stablecoin-scope opinion dates the ESMA position.

event: Notification S.O. 1072(E): five virtual digital asset activities notified under the PMLA (exchange between VDAs and fiat currencies; exchange between VDAs; transfer; safekeeping or administration; participation in and provision of financial services related to an issuer's offer and sale). Read in FIU-IND's 15 September 2025 circular and 8 January 2026 guidelines, which cite it.
source_date: cited in FIU-IND documents of 2025-09-15 and 2026-01-08
effect_on_opinion: Scope. Defines the reporting-entity perimeter an India-scope opinion describes.

event: Order 08/DIR/FIU-IND/2024, Peken Global Limited (KuCoin): penalty of Rs 34,50,000.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dated enforcement event.

event: Order 10/DIR/FIU-IND/2024, Binance: penalty of Rs 18,82,00,000.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dated enforcement event.

event: Order 15/DIR/FIU-IND/2024, Bybit Fintech Limited: penalty of Rs 9,27,00,000. The orders index page prints 2024; the order itself is dated 31 January 2025.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dated enforcement event.

event: Order 16/DIR/FIU-IND/2024, Coinbase India Private Limited: a warning with directions under s.13(2)(a) PMLA, no monetary penalty. The index page prints 2024; the order is dated 6 March 2025.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dated enforcement event, never described as a penalty.

event: Annual Report 2024-25: 49 VDA service providers registered as on 31 March 2025 (45 onshore, 4 offshore); penalties of Rs 28 crore on VDA service providers in FY 2024-25; FIU-IND describes itself as the single authority for registering and AML/CFT monitoring of VDA service providers.
effect_on_opinion: Date. The baseline count and enforcement total, on the report's own date.

event: Third revision of the circular for registration of VDA service providers as reporting entities (F.No. 9-8/2023/COMPL/FIU-IND-Pt-II): failure to register is itself a non-compliance with the PMLA that attracts action under s.13(2); an in-person meeting is part of the process; VDA takes its meaning from s.2(47A) of the Income-tax Act 1961.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. An India-scope opinion dated after 15 September 2025 addresses registration under this revision. Registration is a PMLA obligation, not a licence, an approval or an endorsement.

event: Notification G.S.R. 843(E) (Gazette CG-DL-E-14112025-267647) commences the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 in three tranches: on publication, ss.1(2), 2, 18 to 26, 35, 38 to 43, 44(1) and (3); one year after publication, s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d) (13 November 2026, derived); eighteen months after publication, ss.3 to 5, 6(1) to (8) and (10), 7 to 17, 27 except (1)(d), 28 to 34, 36, 37 and 44(2) (13 May 2027, derived).
effect_on_opinion: Date. Data-fiduciary duties for an Indian counterparty take effect with the eighteen-month tranche. The two derived dates are arithmetic, not stated in the notification.

event: AML and CFT Guidelines for reporting entities providing VDA services (updated as on 8 January 2026): obligations are activity-based and apply irrespective of physical presence in India; the Travel Rule carries the originator's PAN and allows no post-facto submission; dealings in anonymity-enhancing crypto tokens are "not permissible"; VDA is still defined by s.2(47A) of the 1961 Act. Parliament cites this document as the registration framework.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. The document an India-scope opinion covers after 8 January 2026. Its definition still points to the 1961 Act, repealed from 1 April 2026, a dating point the opinion notes.

event: Budget 2026-27: Finance Bill 2026 clause 87 proposes a substituted s.446 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 with a penalty for the s.509 crypto-asset statement (Rs 200 per day; Rs 50,000 for inaccuracy or a due-diligence failure), effective 1 April 2026. A Lok Sabha answer of 10 August 2026 (Unstarred Question 3579) refers to the Finance Act, 2026 as enacted; the enacted text is unverified.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A reporting obligation with a proposed penalty, marked unverified as enacted law until the Finance Act 2026 text is read.

event: Unstarred Question 1986: as of January 2026, 52 offshore VDA service providers had been issued notices under s.13 of the PMLA, with access disallowed under s.79(3)(b) of the IT Act; no delisting guideline exists for privacy coins.
effect_on_opinion: Date. An enforcement figure on its own date, kept separate from the 30 March 2026 takedown list.

event: Income-tax Rules, 2026 notified, replacing the 1962 Rules, in force from 1 April 2026 (Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3579, 10 August 2026). The rule and form for the s.509 statement are unverified.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dating fact for any India-scope opinion that cites the Rules.

regulator: Lok Sabha (Minister of State for Finance)
event: Unstarred Question 5805: 54 VDA service providers registered with FIU-IND as on 9 March 2026 (Annexure I; nine marked not operational, three conditionally onboarded); 53 offshore platforms directed for takedown (Annexure II); no public portal. The answer states that publishing a public list may create the impression that registered entities are licensed, approved or endorsed by the government.
effect_on_opinion: Date. FIU-IND publishes no register, so a credential naming an Indian counterparty records the registration evidence it saw and its date.

event: The Income-tax Act, 2025 comes into force (s.1(3); assent 21 August 2025; Gazette CG-DL-E-22082025-265620). Section 2(111)(d) extends "virtual digital asset" to any crypto-asset on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger; s.509 creates the crypto-asset reporting statement. The short title is the Income-tax Act, 2025, not "(No. 2)".
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. An India-scope opinion dated after 1 April 2026 cites the 2025 Act; FIU-IND's 8 January 2026 guidelines still point to the repealed 1961 definition.

event: Press release 56/2026 and its FAQ: Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenised corporate bonds on a private, permissioned DLT owned by the depositories; the token is the corporate bond and remains a security under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956; the depositories hold the private keys.
effect_on_opinion: Context. India's tokenisation reference point. SEBI has published no crypto-asset stance this tracker can cite.

event: Compliance orders page: no order against a VDA service provider dated 2026 is listed; the 2025 heading holds three bank orders. A negative row, re-checked each edition.
effect_on_opinion: Date. An absence stated with its date.

event: GENIUS Act enacted (S. 1582). Section 20: effective on the earlier of 18 months after enactment (18 January 2027 by arithmetic) or 120 days after the final implementing regulations.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. Enacted, not in effect. The SEC's 17 March 2026 interpretation records that a payment stablecoin issued by a permitted payment stablecoin issuer is excluded from the definition of a security.

event: Notice of proposed rulemaking implementing the GENIUS Act (comments to 1 May 2026).
effect_on_opinion: Date. Implementing rules in flight.

event: Memorandum of Understanding (Release 2026-26): a Joint Harmonization Initiative, including clarifying product definitions through joint interpretations and rulemakings.
effect_on_opinion: Date. Product definitions may move by joint act; an opinion dates its reading.

event: Interpretation, Releases 33-11412 and 34-105020 (effective 23 March 2026; 91 FR 13714): five categories of crypto asset (digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, stablecoins, digital securities). The first three "are not themselves securities", and a non-security crypto asset can still be offered and sold subject to an investment contract. Supersedes the 2019 staff Framework (footnote 21); the CFTC will administer the Commodity Exchange Act consistently with it.
effect_on_opinion: Scope and date. A US-scope opinion issued before 17 March 2026 was written against a superseded framework.

event: CFTC staff FAQs on crypto assets and blockchain technologies first issued 20 March 2026; the 24 September 2026 update (press release 9303-26) adds tokenised permitted investments and blockchain recordkeeping.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dating fact.

event: Regulation Crypto Assets proposed (Releases 33-11434 and 34-106150; 91 FR 54510): exemptions of up to $5 million over four years and $75 million per 12 months, and a conditional carve-out under which a crypto asset would be deemed not to be subject to an investment contract; antifraud provisions still apply. Comments due on or before 20 October 2026 (open on 11 October 2026).
effect_on_opinion: Date. A proposal, not a rule, and never read as a live carve-out.

event: Statement: the Senate cloture vote on the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) failed; only Congress can provide lasting legal certainty. A single official source; the tally is unverified.
effect_on_opinion: Scope. No market-structure statute as of 11 October 2026.

event: Innovation Exemption for tokenized NMS stock (Release 2026-90; order 34-106402): temporary conditional relief for Tokenized Securities Venues for five years, with smart contracts that are auditable, public and deployed on a public, permissionless distributed ledger.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dating fact for tokenised securities.

event: Interim final rule on forms and procedures for the review of state certifications (effective 30 September 2026; comments to 30 November 2026). Earlier GENIUS Act steps: FinCEN and OFAC proposals published 10 April 2026; FDIC proposals published 10 April and 5 June 2026; Treasury proposal on issuance, offer and sale 18 August 2026 (comments to 19 October 2026).
effect_on_opinion: Date. The GENIUS implementation timeline; the Section 20 effective-date contingency remains.

event: Proposal on adviser and fund custody of crypto assets (Release 2026-100; Federal Register 6 October 2026; 60-day comment period): self-custody under certain circumstances; state trust companies as custodians.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A dating fact.

event: Advance notice of proposed rulemaking, Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (press release 9307-26), on s.2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act; published in the Federal Register on 13 October 2026 (91 FR 64811, document 2026-20888); comments to 14 December 2026.
effect_on_opinion: Date. A CFTC framework at the pre-proposal stage; an opinion dates its CFTC reading.
